item.title: Solved: Mastering the Python Send Function in Generators
item.description:
What is the send Function in Python Generators?

The send function in Python generators plays a critical role in facilitating two-way communication between the generator and the caller. Unlike a standard function, which executes and returns a value once, a generator function can yield multiple values over time, effectively pausing its state until it is resumed.

How Does send Work?

The send(value) method resumes generator execution and sends a value into it. The provided value becomes the output from the current yield statement. Importantly, send() will return the next yielded value from the generator, or raise a StopIteration exception if the generator has completed its execution.

item.title: Solved: Understanding the Yield Keyword in Python
item.description:
The yield keyword in Python plays a fundamental role in creating generator functions, allowing for a more memory-efficient iteration compared to traditional lists. Let’s dive deep into what yield does, backed up by code examples, alternative approaches, and practical use cases.

What Does the Yield Keyword Do?

When you define a function that includes the yield statement, it transforms the function into a generator. Unlike a regular function that terminates and returns a single value, a generator pauses its execution when yield is used, providing a value to the caller, and retains its state for the next invocation.
